about: Synthetic test cases for the weighting-experiment-metrics skill. Each case feeds the skill a leadership context and (optionally) experiment deltas, then asserts observable expected behavior. Cases tagged deterministic=true have a fixed correct index/decision and double as regression checks; others test reasoning quality (phase mapping, constraint enforcement, guardrail gating).

cases.query: Help me set Success Index weights for our next experiment.
expected_behavior: Runs Step 1 and ASKS for maturity phase / strategic priority before proposing any numbers
Asks about drag risk tolerance (attrition vs bad debt vs technical)
Does not fabricate a phase; if forced, states an explicit assumption

cases.query: We're a seed-stage SaaS in a land-grab. Top priority is signing as many new logos as possible this quarter; churn and billing issues are tolerable for now. Recommend weights.
expected_behavior: Maps to Market Capture and anchors on w1=0.5 (acquisition dominant)
Returned w1+w2+w3 == 1.0
Every pi >= 1.0
One-line justification per weight

cases.query: Mature platform, big installed base. Goal this year is expansion revenue and upsell. We are very sensitive to uncollected/bad debt because finance got burned last year. Set weights.
expected_behavior: Maps to Monetization; w2 dominant
p2 (bad balances) is the largest penalty given finance sensitivity
Sum of w == 1.0; all pi >= 1.0

cases.query: We have a churn problem and reliability complaints. This year is all about retention and product stability. Recommend the weighting matrix.
expected_behavior: Maps to Product Health; w3 dominant
p3 (technical friction) elevated (>= 2.5)
Sum of w == 1.0; all pi >= 1.0

cases.query: Approach 3 weights are set: w1=0.2, w2=0.2, w3=0.6, p1=2.0, p2=1.0, p3=2.5. Experiment results: Onboarding Milestone +15%, Acquisition +3%, Technical Friction +1%, everything else flat. Guardrails all clear. Score it.
expected_behavior: Shows substituted arithmetic = 0.6 + 0 + 9.0 - 2.5
Computes index = +7.1
Decision = DEPLOY

cases.query: Approach 2 weights: w1=0.2, w2=0.5, w3=0.3, p1=2.0, p2=3.0, p3=1.0. Results: Expansion +14%, Bad Balances +4%, Technical Friction +2%, rest flat. Guardrails clear. Score it.
expected_behavior: Shows arithmetic = 0 + 7.0 + 0 - 12.0 - 2.0
Computes index = -7.0
Decision = REJECT and explicitly names the volume mirage (+14% expansion drained by bad-debt penalty)

cases.query: Approach 1 weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.2, w3=0.3, p1=3.0, p2=1.5, p3=1.0. Results look great: Acquisition +20%, no drags. BUT the SRM Chi-squared canary fired at p=0.0004. Score it.
expected_behavior: Checks Layer 1 guardrail FIRST
Recognizes SRM p=0.0004 < 0.001 breach
Declares the index null and void; verdict INVALID; sample discarded
Does NOT report a positive DEPLOY despite the +20% acquisition

cases.query: Approach 1 weights: w1=0.5, w2=0.2, w3=0.3, p1=3.0, p2=1.5, p3=1.0. Results: Acquisition +12%, no drags, index is positive. SRM is clean (p=0.5) but support ticket volume jumped +28% over baseline. Score it.
expected_behavior: Computes positive index (0.5*12 = +6.0)
Recognizes +28% support-ticket spike breaches the >15% operational ceiling
Verdict = FREEZE for manual executive review rather than auto-DEPLOY

cases.query: Approach 2. Our product uses 3-day deferred invoices, and bad-debt only shows in the DB ~30-45 days later. We ran a 7-day test: Expansion +9%, all drags currently flat. Score it and tell me if I can trust it.
expected_behavior: Computes a positive index from the +9% expansion
Flags Backlog gap #3 (reporting lag): bad-debt/attrition may not have landed in a 7-day window
Recommends a lag-correction coefficient or a data-maturation freeze before finalizing rollout
Treats the DEPLOY signal as low-confidence rather than final

cases.query: We're mostly in growth but starting to care about retention too — call it 70% acquisition focus, 30% keep-them-happy. Attrition is our scariest risk. Give me weights.

leadership_context.priority: blend: acquisition-leaning with emerging retention focus

expected_behavior: Anchors on Market Capture but shifts some weight toward w3 (milestone/retention)
Returned w1+w2+w3 == 1.0 after adjustment (states the normalization)
p1 (attrition) is the dominant penalty and all pi >= 1.0
Notes the blend explicitly in justifications
